conviction_note: RLX gives no guidance and the options chain gives no implied move, so the print turns on two things the stock has paid for before. First, capital return: the Q3 2025 release declared a US$0.10/ADS dividend and the stock rose 10.3%; the Q2 2025 release declared one and the stock rose 7.1%; the Q2 2026 release declared none and the stock fell 3.0%. Second, the first quarter with the European distributor consolidated, measured against a consensus (net income about RMB304m) that sits well above Q2's RMB222m. The stock is at a 52-week low and below its cash, which gives a mild positive lean (p_up 55). abs_move_pct is 5, above the cleaned median of 3.0, because this release can carry a dividend decision and is the first consolidated quarter. The +1.1 findings sum and the +0.5 scaled number agree in sign; the scaled number is smaller because the dividend is inferred from a pattern that Q2 2026 broke.

The revenue bar of about +55% YoY rests on the size of an undisclosed distributor (51% stake, consolidated from Q3), so the headline revenue line is soft and the sizes on it are capped small.

findings.finding: The Q3 release is where RLX has declared its yearly dividend, and those prints were the stock's two largest up-moves. Q3 2024 (Nov 2024) declared $0.01/ADS. Q3 2025 (2025-11-14) declared $0.10/ADS and the stock rose 10.3%. Q2 2025 declared $0.01 and the stock rose 7.1%. Q2 2026 declared none and the stock fell 3.0%. A repeat $0.10 would be a 6.8% yield at $1.465. The balance sheet supports it: US$2.05bn of cash and investments at 2026-06-30 against a market value of about $1.8bn, plus about $170m left under the buyback extended to 2027-12-31. Two facts argue against a repeat: no dividend came with Q2 2026, and the Q3 distributor purchase used cash at an undisclosed price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prints with a dividend declaration: +10.3% (2025-11-14, $0.10) and +7.14% (2025-08-22, $0.01). Prints without one: -3.0% (2026-08-14), 0.0% (2026-05-20), -0.88% (2026-03-13). The buyback extension on 2025-12-31 moved the stock +1.75%.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is -8.4% month to date and at a 52-week low just above $1.40, trading below cash per ADS (about $1.67 on 1.226bn weighted ADS). If the market expected a 6-7% cash payout it would not be making new lows into the record date season. Coverage is two to six analysts and no preview mentions the dividend.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print weak and under its own cash. It is -6.1% over 5 days, -10.7% over 20 days and -36.7% year to date, at $1.465 against a 52-week range of $1.40-$2.585 and an average target of about $2.81. Cash, deposits and investments were US$2.05bn (RMB13,883m) at 2026-06-30 against about 1.226bn weighted ADS, roughly $1.67 per ADS. The bar for a relief move is low, but cheapness alone is not a catalyst.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026 prints came in on a falling stock and drew 0.0 to -3.0%. The low did not attract buyers at those prints without a capital-return trigger.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price itself, so it is partly priced by definition. The asymmetry is that a stock at its low and under its cash has little room for a disappointment sell-off unless the quarter is bad. A market braced for good news would show a run-up into the print; this one shows a run-down.
findings.independence: Cash figure: https://finviz.com/news/382239/rlx-technology-announces-unaudited-second-quarter-2026-financial-results (company release). The price path is in the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: The consensus bar for consolidated profit is high against Q2. MarketScreener has Q3 net income RMB304m, EBIT RMB213m and EPS RMB0.25; Chartmill has EPS RMB0.23. Q2 2026 was GAAP net income RMB222.0m, GAAP operating income RMB130.4m and non-GAAP EPS per ADS RMB0.178. Q2 also had an operating cash outflow of RMB63m. Clearing the bar needs a 37% QoQ jump in net income from a 51%-owned, lower-margin distributor plus organic growth, while management guided gross margin down from 35.4%. Revenue consensus (RMB1.75-1.77bn, +55% YoY) depends on the undisclosed size of the distributor, so a headline revenue beat or miss mostly reflects consolidation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 was scored as an EPS miss ($0.03 against $0.09, FMP snippet) and the stock fell 3.0%. Q1 2026 was scored as an EPS beat (about 24%) and the stock was flat. The stock's response to the profit line is muted.
findings.why_not_priced: Two to six analysts cover the stock and Chartmill shows revenue estimates revised up 8.55% in three months, which suggests the consolidation is modelled generously. If the market believed the RMB304m, a stock trading at about 5x that annualised ex-cash would not be at its low. The bar and the price disagree, and one of them is stale.
findings.independence: Chartmill EPS RMB0.23 and revenue RMB1.765bn (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/RLX/estimates, snippet). Q2 actuals: https://finviz.com/news/382239/rlx-technology-announces-unaudited-second-quarter-2026-financial-results. The two estimate sources are separate; this finding shares the Q2 release with finding 2.

findings.finding: On the 2026-08-14 call management pre-announced the Q3 shape. Gross margin will 'settle back' from 35.4%, which it called a 'temporary product and revenue mix shift'. The European distributor 'operates on a lower percentage gross margin profile' but will 'meaningfully expand our operating profit and net profit scale'. Mainland China will be 'broadly flat' for the full year. A Q3 gross margin drop is therefore inside what the company told the market to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin printed 31.8% in Q1 2026 (stock 0.0%) and 35.4% in Q2 2026 (stock -3.0%). The stock has not traded on the margin line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced, because it was said on the call. What stays open is how far the margin falls: a print in the mid-20s from distributor mix would read worse than 'settle back' implies.
findings.independence: 2Firsts on the same release: https://www.2firsts.com/news/2firsts-exclusive-analysis--rlx-q2-revenue-rises-148-company-takes-control-of-western-european-distributor-and-expands-multi-category-strategy. Same underlying event, so it is not independent of the transcript.

findings.finding: Chinese customs data show Q3 2026 vape-related exports to the UK at $461.8m, +21.6% YoY: August $177.1m (+51.4%) and September $123.9m (+37.4%). That points to stocking ahead of the UK Vaping Products Duty that started 2026-10-01. Total exports went from July +16.5% to September -6.3% YoY. Indonesia rose about $22.7m and South Korea +37.9%; the EU-27 was -0.5%, with Germany lower. For RLX, the UK is the market of its suspected May 2025 acquisition (Totally Wicked, unconfirmed). Pre-duty loading would flatter Q3 international revenue and weigh on Q4 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The pre-stocking quarter of Q1 2026 (export-rebate change) printed +96% YoY revenue and the stock moved 0.0%. The market discounted the one-off.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an industry series dominated by US-bound disposables and OEMs, and nobody has tied it to RLX's UK mix. It is a proxy: RLX's own share of these flows is not disclosed, so the size is small.
findings.independence: UK duty start date 2026-10-01: https://rri.co.id/surabaya/internasional/2244229/excise-duty-stamps-for-vape-products-in-the-uk-what-indonesia-can-learn. RLX's UK link via Totally Wicked (unconfirmed): https://www.2firsts.com/news/uks-leading-e-cigarette-retailer-totally-wicked-acquired-actual-controller-suspected-to-be-relx-affiliated-company-2

findings.finding: On 2026-10-12, after the last call, China's Announcement No. 29 removed export VAT rebates on vape devices, empty pods and nicotine from 2027-04-01. That follows the April 2026 removal on nicotine inhalation products, which gave RLX a disclosed one-time Q1 2026 benefit from partner pre-stocking. Management will have to address a 2027 margin headwind and a possible pre-stocking Q1 2027 on this call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 one-time export-policy benefit drew a 0.0% reaction, and Q2's normalisation from it drew -3.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: The policy is public, but RLX has not spoken since it was announced. Q2 gross margin rose to 35.4% after the first rebate removal, so the cost to RLX is ambiguous and the market has no company read yet.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 one-time export benefit, company release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001828365/000110465926064175/tm2615066d1_ex99-1.htm

findings.finding: Smoore (6969.HK), a Shenzhen vape hardware maker, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-12. Revenue was RMB3,946m, -6.0% YoY and +17.7% QoQ; enterprise-customer revenue was RMB3,143m, -8.4% YoY; profit was RMB365m, +15.2% YoY. Growth came from US flavoured products and heated tobacco, not Europe. The sector is soft YoY, with QoQ recovery in Q3.
findings.link: Same industry and city (Shenzhen e-vapor manufacturing). RLX makes its own devices, and no shared customer or supply relationship is stated. Smoore's growth is US/HNB-driven while RLX is Asia/Europe and does not sell commercially in the US. Effectively none stated.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and weakly linked, so it is filed small for the judges.
